doc.title: Herbie Hancock interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 18, 1995

title: The Rhythm of Life Foundation: technology for humanity
summary: He describes his new foundation, urging technology to serve humanity and responsibility.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: And the idea of the foundation, the overview pertains to technology for humanity. Because I’ve noticed that the world of technology is going through the roof. It’s amazing the things that are possible. And the importance that technology is going to play in education, in entertainment — and they’ve coined this word called edutainment you

know, it makes education fun — and communications and also in the workplace for business — teleconferencing, for home entertainment, television, telephone — I mean all these things are going to be really linked up together in the very near future.

The foundation is called The Rhythm of Life Foundation. And I look at programs like CNN and other news programs and I see what’s happening to humanity. Humanity is in pretty bad shape you know. And so I’m thinking, something’s wrong with this picture. If the measure of the value of something, isn’t it supposed to be what it does for humanity? It should be that anyway. Then what is technology doing for humanity if humanity is in the toilet and technology is going through the roof? So there is something wrong with that picture and so I think there needs to be a lot more balance between the typical approach to technology, which is to look at machines first and figure out what kind of tools can we make from these machines? Then takes those tools to human beings and say how can you use these? And the human being says oh I can use it for this or for that. Meanwhile, the real issues that are the real problems for human beings which have to do with the fact that responsibility, which is something that’s part of the fiber of life, that’s almost totally lacking in society today, and across the board, with adults and with our young people, a sense of responsibility. Things like courage, self worth, mutual respect, you name it, I mean so many of these things need to be nurtured, need to be encouraged, and even the decision making process you know, this idea of having a very short view of life needs to be re-examined and changed so we have a much longer view so we can have a sense of the results of what the results of our actions can lead to. Promoting that kind of follow through and thinking about your life. So anyway, what this foundation wants to do is to propose that the technical, technological community spent at least some kind of balance of time looking at humanity first and saying how can I use technology to address the needs of humanity? And develop software and ideas from that standpoint.
